title: Circles Builds: Sklar Bikes PBJ – John Watson
content:
Last week, we looked at the Nagoya-based Circles bike shop in Japan. As supporting content, today we’re featuring a recent Sklar Bikes PBJ build that just rolled out of the shop for a customer…

Sklar Bikes PBJ

The PBJ makes a lot of sense as a multi-functioning mixed-terrain bicycle. Ten years ago, I commissioned Adam Sklar to build me a bike for desert touring. That custom titanium tourer started the Sklar Bikes PBJ lineage. Last year, in 2025, I reviewed Adam’s Taiwanese-produced PBJ model after riding it on a quick bike tour around Mount Tam in the Bay Area.

Here in New Mexico, I’ve taken my Desert Moose, the nickname the bike earned on one desert outing, on local overnighters as well as the Northern New Mexico CDT. It’s a true-to-form forever bike for me. Perfect for Canyon Country, the Mojave, and beyond. All this to say, I’m intimately familiar with the PBJ. If you’d like to learn more about the PBJ, read my review in the Radavist archives below.

The team at Circles have built up several PBJ frames over the past few years. Here are a few above, taken from the Ridealive Beautiful Bicycles gallery. The PBJ is best equipped with racks, since it has provisions for bolt-on cargo carriers, versus other bikes sans rack mounts that often rely on floppy bikepacking bags.

Circles Build

While I spent the afternoon prying into each shelf and display case at Circles, Makoto sat at his wheel-building station, zeroed in on a wheel build. First, he cut the spokes, then he prepped them before pulling a pair of Astral Serpentine rims from a box above the mechanics area in the small but organized Circles work area.

“Makoto!” I exclaimed, excited to see my friend again. “John-san!” he replied. We exchanged hugs and memories from our 2016 bike tour around Mount Fuji and on to Izu Oshima. After briefly catching up, he was back to work, lacing the spokes through the Chris King hub. Hours passed, and I’d finished documenting the Circles shop just as he was finishing the wheels.

The following day, I returned to Circles after documenting the Circles Tailored store, as well as a few custom builds to Makoto, putting the finishing touches on this silver Sklar PBJ; the home for those wheels. Every cable was perfectly routed, every t-crossed, and i-dotted. I asked if I could document the bike. Before I could roll it out of the shop, an employee came over with some cleaner and wiped down the handlebars.

Balleur Kit

Looking at this build, it exemplifies Circle’s Modus Operandi: supporting a mix of Japanese and Domestic US manufacturers, splurging on balleur parts, and hanging them on a comparatively approachable frameset. If this had been a custom Sklar bike, it’d be two or three times the price. Paul Component cranks, Boxcar stem, Klampers, Canti Levers, Taco Pedals, Sklar PBJ bars, a Shovel Research TC-1 top cap, and a friction Shimano Deore mech complement the Astral and Chris King build kit, making for one happy customer.

Circles and Circles Tailored roll builds like this out of small, well-organized workshops all days of the week, and this customer has to be stoked to be putting miles on it.

If you’re in Japan and would like a similar build, holler at Circles and let Makoto cook you up something delicious like this.

See the PBJ specs at Sklar Bikes.
